adrs.title: UOR Mechanics — The Exact Math of Prime-Indexing
adrs.context: Mutable file-path identity permits duplication, reordering, and platform-dependent drift; UOR requires collision-free, compositionally rich, exactly reproducible identity across heterogeneous nodes.
adrs.decision: Adopt prime-indexing as the canonical UOR substrate. Irreducible identity: a prime is the invariant identity of a node; composites encode relations. Exponents as memory (OFA-ii): k_i in n = product p_i^k_i is a surplus ledger; primes accumulate monotonically (p to p^2 to p^3). Lawful composition: K1 ⊗ K2 = lcm(K1, K2) as a lossless structural join preventing duplication. Multiplicative union: K1 ⊕ K2 = product over p of p^(v_p(K1) + v_p(K2)). Zero-drift architecture: exact rational arithmetic only, no floating point. Cryptographic verification: Binary Canonical Serialization (fixed field orders, ULEB128 prefixes) and Poseidon2 ZK sealing (t=9, r=8). Call-market cleavage (Holotrade, phase-gated): Fee = 1/10 * DeltaP; node yield = ask + 9/10 * DeltaP, with receipt-locked ledger finality.
consequences: State is never identified by mutable path; one prime-indexed ledger drives identity, history, and compensation
Merges are lossless and deduplicating (lcm); unions are exact (exponent addition)
BCS + Poseidon2 sealing make receipts tamper-evident and cross-platform (Rust/Lean)
Banned floats foreclose drift and penny-shaving settlement attacks
Implemented substrate: ADR-0013 canonical BCS wire format and PWEH integrity chain

adrs.title: Symmetry-Matched Polarization Analysis in MnF2
adrs.context: Unpolarized inelastic neutron scattering on MnF2 reported no resolvable altermagnetic magnon band splitting within resolution, while polarized INS later accessed an antisymmetric dynamical channel and reported a domain-dependent chiral response: different measurement operations, not contradictions. A null in one channel must not be treated as physical absence in another.
adrs.decision: Adopt symmetry-matched polarization analysis as the interpretive discipline for altermagnetic neutron-scattering claims in MnF2: decompose the transverse dynamical magnetic correlation tensor via the Blume-Maleev cross section into polarization-even and odd parts so that reversing incident neutron polarization isolates the antisymmetric (chiral) correlator; classify nulls into the four-null taxonomy (physical, resolution, polarization-projection, antiferromagnetic-domain cancellation), deliberately contextual rather than exhaustive; require a resolvability criterion that states which channel each null belongs to and declares the anti-ferromagnetic domain state for domain-sensitive readout.
consequences: Unpolarized null results are located in the taxonomy rather than overruling polarized signatures
Spectral resolution and chiral sensitivity are kept as separate design axes
Every null claim carries an explicit stage of loss, making comparisons falsifiable
Provides the channel separation on which the dJ7 source-sector, reversal-space and probe-tensor work items build

adrs.title: The dJ7 Principle - Symmetry-Complement Source Sectors in Altermagnetic MnF2
adrs.context: A Hamiltonian term small in total energy can be leading in a selected symmetry channel. In MnF2 a small imbalance between the two symmetry-distinct seventh-neighbor Heisenberg exchange bonds (J7a, J7b) is a candidate source coordinate for the altermagnetic chiral response; whether the construction is valid depends on a precise group-theoretic statement relative to a declared reference model.
adrs.decision: Adopt the dJ7 principle as the canonical account of symmetry-complement source sectors in altermagnetic MnF2: group averaging over a reference group G0 defines a projector onto the invariant subspace and splits V = im P XOR ker P into invariant sector and symmetry-complement source sector; a coefficient lambda in the complement obeys the covariance F_O(rho_s lambda) = chi_O(s) F_O(lambda), and under rho_s = -I the odd response has only odd total degree F(lambda) = k*lambda + O(||lambda||^3) (selection, not amplification); the source is the inequivalence dJ7 = J7b - J7a of the seventh-neighbor bonds with the bond-label convention declared explicitly; the result is a bounded-range-seven near-scalar, not a universal one-dimensional coordinate.
consequences: Source attribution is tied to a declared reference model and bond convention, preventing tautological complement definitions
The odd-channel expansion fixes the scaling of the chiral response, enabling falsifiability
Substrate for reversal-space tomography and probe-tensor correspondence
Explicitly warns against exporting dJ7 as a universal weak coordinate to other altermagnets

adrs.title: Reversal-Space Tomography of Weak Altermagnetic Exchange in MnF2
adrs.context: The dJ7 principle identifies a few-micro-eV seventh-neighbor exchange imbalance coexisting with a larger dipolar contribution in MnF2. adrs.decision: Adopt reversal-space tomography as the engineering framework for signed readouts of weak altermagnetic exchange in MnF2: treat partner momentum, field sign, incident polarization, and magnetic-domain sign as binary design coordinates of a (Z2)^N reversal experiment; decompose the measured response into exact Walsh-Hadamard factorial contrasts; interpret contrasts as characters of the physical (Z2)^N reversal group only after a path-consistency gate (reversals are independent involutions ri^2 ~ I, ri rj ~ rj ri); treat a significant coefficient in a model-forbidden parity sector as an obstruction channel exposing leakage or missing physics; measure dJ7 as a signed quantity only after the bond-label convention is fixed.
consequences: Weak-exchange readouts become certifiably signed and falsifiable
Gain in transduction is made explicit without claiming the coefficient is large
Hysteresis and path-dependent preparation are admitted and tested by the path-consistency gate
Supplies the operational readout protocol for the dJ7 source-sector and its singular echo in the target-first calculus

adrs.title: Static Multipolar Order and Dynamical Chiral Response in MnF2 - Probe-Tensor Correspondence
adrs.context: MnF2 evidence spans elastic multipole reconstruction (anisotropic Mn magnetization, ligand spin polarization, a symmetry-allowed rank-5 magnetic multipole) and inelastic magnon chirality. Symmetry may relate these objects, but they are generated by different forward maps, and identifiability between them is conditional, not automatic.
adrs.decision: Adopt the probe-tensor correspondence as the discipline relating static multipolar and dynamical chiral claims in MnF2: keep Hamiltonian coordinates, equilibrium one-point magnetization tensors, static response tensors, connected correlations, and the probe/instrument map as distinct objects; a static multipole-rank functional fK is identifiable from a dynamical chiral measurement Mchi only if fK = fK-bar circle pi_Mchi, which symmetry compatibility alone does not establish; treat rank identifiability as conditional on a declared basis, radial/form-factor model, origin convention, nuisance space, and domain state; model uncontrolled domain ensembles explicitly because a vanishing one-point moment can coexist with finite diffraction intensity.
consequences: Static-rank and dynamical-chirality results are kept as separate propositions, preventing cross-tensor claim migration
Every multipole reconstruction states its conditioning assumptions or is not closed
Domain ensemble and cancellation effects are handled explicitly
Establishes the K component of the six-element claim vector

adrs.title: Symmetry-Complement Coordinates Across Altermagnets - Cross-Material Falsification
adrs.context: A portable symmetry argument must survive materials in which the microscopic hierarchy, probe physics, and even the magnetic state differ, and must not be made true by choosing its reference model after seeing the target response. adrs.decision: Adopt the hardened cross-material falsification benchmark with a six-component claim vector c = (M, S, E, chi, R, K): static magnetic order, response-specific Hamiltonian/operator source sector, nonrelativistic electronic spin splitting, chiral collective dynamics, a signed reversal/control relation, and static multipolar content; accept source-sector attribution only relative to a predeclared or independently anchored reference (H0, G0) for which the target channel is absent or symmetry-degenerate, with certificate A = A-ind AND A-state AND A-null AND A-no-retune; require a measurement-map statement, the dual counterfactual, mechanism specificity challenges, and independent closure; enforce the source-state gate so a contradicted bulk state (e.g. RuO2) blocks downstream source attribution; include MnSi as a non-altermagnetic specificity control so chi != 0 does not imply an altermagnetic source.
consequences: The restricted source-sector principle survives while the universal one-dimensional coordinate, universal smallness ratio, and the inference chi != 0 -> altermagnetic source are rejected
Attribution stops at the source-state gate before downstream observables count
MnF2 is the near-scalar calibration (dS ~ 1), MnTe/CrSb need broader sectors (dS > 1), FeF2 separates dipolar and altermagnetic sources, bulk RuO2 is blocked upstream

adrs.title: When Null Does Not Mean Absent - Measurement-Map Geometry and Null-Witness Duality
adrs.context: A null experimental outcome is not by itself a statement of physical absence: a latent state passes through source physics, response formation, probe selection, ensemble averaging, instrument transfer, and nuisance structure before data exist. Stage labels such as response null or projection null are often assigned without a rigorous basis.
adrs.decision: Adopt the layered measurement-map geometry with null-witness duality: factor the total map M = T A P R S over source/state, response, probe projection, ensemble/domain averaging, and transfer/resolution; define observational equivalence by measurement fibers; in a layered linear experiment with cumulative maps Fj record the cumulative null filtration Kj = ker Fj and dual witness spaces Wj = Ann(Kj) = im Fj*; treat the total observational quotient as factorization-independent while stage-local null attribution is invariant only under invertible reparameterizations of declared intermediate spaces, not under arbitrary refactorization; a target C is identifiable after stage j iff Kj is subset of ker C with obstruction dimension dC(A) = dim C(ker A); passive post-processing cannot restore an erased distinction, whereas active intervention creates a new measurement map; combine independent probes by kernel intersection only under a common latent state; extend to nonlinear/noisy (nuisance-projected Jacobians, Fisher information), stochastic (outcome distributions), and quantum (POVM probability maps) measurements.
consequences: Every null is attributed to a declared stage or its label is withheld
A large raw signal can be non-identifying while a null channel coexists with a nonzero orthogonal-sector signal
Upstream source contradiction is distinct from a downstream projection null
Reversal channels double as obstruction testbeds

adrs.title: Target-First Observability Calculus - Admissible Ambiguity and Dual Obstructions
adrs.context: Experimental design is often organized around an available instrument rather than the claim the data support. A high-amplitude measurement can have zero target design gain while a much smaller measurement exactly closes the target; design must work backward from the claim.
adrs.decision: Adopt the target-first observability calculus: specify the target, prerequisite state, and state gate before the forward map; for exact common-state linear measurements define residual structural ambiguity OC(E) = C(ker AE) with closure when {0}, structural design gain DeltaC(B|E) = dC(E) - dC(E union B) >= 0, and report exact closure separately from admissible-set contraction OC(E; y, Omega) with width wC; any v in ker AE with Cv != 0 is a constructive dual counterexample, and the most useful next experiment is one maximally sensitive to it; place the target in an allowed parity sector while recording model-forbidden sectors as obstruction channels; after structural viability, optimize practical margin with nuisance-projected Jacobians (c-optimal / goal-oriented OED downstream); enforce the rule that a downstream response cannot repair a contradicted upstream source state; publish per-claim target, state gate, forward map, nuisance variables, an explicit target-changing ambiguity, reversal/complementary probe, conditioning diagnostic, and an attempted falsification.
consequences: Experiment selection is justified by target design gain or contraction, not raw amplitude
Exact closure and quantitative contraction are reported separately
A 13-step protocol governs claim production and publication

For MnF2 three shortcuts are forbidden: magnon splitting alone does not identify signed exchange; a chiral signal does not by symmetry determine static multipole rank; a static multipole reconstruction does not prove another probe's dynamical response
